title: Decoder / demultiplexer
summary: A decoder converts an n-bit binary input to a one-hot output (2^n outputs, exactly one is 1). A 2:4 decoder: outputs D0-D3, where D[i] = 1 if input = i. Demultiplexer (DEMUX) routes a single input to one of 2^n outputs based on select bits. Decoders are used for address decoding, instruction decoding, and one-hot state machines.

Reverse of decoder: outputs the binary code of the highest-priority active input. Used for interrupt priority.

notes: Decoders are used in memory address decoding (chip select), instruction decoding (control unit), and display (7-segment).
A decoder + OR gates can implement any Boolean function (sum of products).
Priority encoders are used in interrupt controllers (highest priority wins).
Decoders are the inverse of encoders (binary to one-hot vs one-hot to binary).
